INTRODUCTION

Where the driving position memorizing option is fitted, the driver's seat and rear view mirrors are equipped with electric motors that allow the adjustment of the position (a movement motor). Each adjustment mechanism is equipped with a sensor that allows the Driver's Position Node (NAG) to identify the position of the seat and the rear view mirrors at any time.

With the assistance of specific memorizing controls, the user can request the memorizing of the driver's posotion and can request that the seat and the rear view mirrors return to a position memorized previously.

This function can be applied:

  • to the driver's seat where the following four movements are memorized: seat forwards-backwards (sliding), seat height adjustment (parallel lifting), seat angle, backrest angle,
  • the two door mirrors where the following movements are memorized: up-down adjustment for each mirror, left-right adjustment for each mirror.

There are two methods for memorizing and recalling the driver's position:

  • memorizing and recall using the memorizing control panel located on the seat,
  • memorizing and recall of the last position using the remote control.

Electrically adjustable heated front seats (where fitted)

The adjustments can only be made with the ignition key in the ON position.

There are 4 levels for the seat heating:

  • 0 (off),
  • 2 (medium heating),
  • 3 (maximum heating),
  • 1 (minimum heating),

To carry out the memorizing, proceed as follows:

  • move the seat to the desired position,
  • press button M on control panel D,
  • press button 1 on control panel D, if the seat position is to be memorized in memory 1,
  • press button 2 on control panel D, if the seat position is to be memorized in memory 2,

The position of the door mirrors is also memorized in conjunction with the seat adjustment.

OPERATION

The principle diagram is illustrated below.

The NAG is electrically connected directly (through special wires) with:

  • memorizing control panel inputs,
  • seat manual control outputs,
  • seat motor control outputs.
  • seat position sensor inputs.

The NAG is connected, via the VAN CAR2 network, with:

  • NBC: Condition of the vehicle (engine running, etc.),
  • door nodes: Position of the rear view mirrrors and manual control.

The NAG carries out:

  • the memorizing of the information in the memories for a position if button M is pressed and then one of the two memory number buttons is pressed,
  • the management of the manual seat controls using the manual control,
  • the operation of the seat activators following a memorizing control,
  • the acquisition of the positions indicated by the seat sensors,
  • the management of the memorizing control panel located on the seat, the memorizing of the position of the seat and the door mirrors.
  • the management of the memorizing control panel located on the seat, the memorizing of the position of the seat and the door mirrors,
  • the VAN interface with the network for controlling the rear view mirrors via the NBC and the driver and passenger door nodes,
  • the fault diagnosis of the system: seat motors and sensors, seat controls, memorizing control panel (when connected to the NAG).

The NBC manages:

  • the authorizations for memory recall and memorizing,
  • the authorizations for automatic or manual memory recall
  • the authorizations for the operation of the seat,
  • the authorizations for the operation of the rear view mirrors.

Procedure for memorizing positions

With the key in position M (driving position) the user U1 makes the adjustment 1 (seat and rear view mirrors) by pressing button 1 and the memorizing by pressing button M and then button 1; similarly, for user 2, position 2, button 2, memorizing M2.

Memorizing a new position cancels the previous one.

Memorizing using remote controls

Memorizing using the remote control consists of memorizing the current position of the seat and the rear view mirrors in the specific areas of the NAG memory known as Me1 and Me2 (irrespective of the control panel memories known as: M1, M2).

The function consists of memorizing the current position of the driver's seat when the user presses the remote control locking button.

The NAG can memorize two positions:

  • Me1, dedicated to current positions known at the time of locking using remote control 1,
  • Me2, dedicated to current positions known at the time of locking using remote control 2,

Procedure for recalling regulation 1 or 2

With the engine switched off: simply press button 1 or 2 briefly to recall the corresponding position memorized. After the same position has been recalled five times in succession, the function is neutralized until the engine is started up.

With the engine running: press button 1 or 2 until a sound signal indicates the end of the adjustment of the position set previously.

Operating strategy

With the key in position M, user U1 carries out adjustment 1 which is memorized (M1) after having pressed button 1 and the remote control becomes T1; each time U1 uses remote control T1 the latter will ensure adjustment 1.

Two remote controls are always supplied with electrically adjustable seats, but if user U2 does not have remote control T2: user U2 opens the vehicle using remote control T1 and when button 2 is pressed this adjusts the seat to position 2 set previously.

The memory recall for the positions memorized in Me1 or Me2 is achieved when the user presses the remote control unlocking button corresponding to the associated memory irrespective of the vehicle locking condition (vehicle locked or unlocked).

The memory recall for the positions memorized in Me1 or Me2 is achieved at the same time as an unlocking when the user has pressed the "luggage compartment opening" button using the remote control (the vehicle was locked previously).

Memory recall authorization conditions

During a memory recall, any operation of the memorizing control panel or a direct control (seat or rear view mirror), stops the seat memory recall procedure (by pressing continuously or impulse recall). If a rear view mirror memory recall has been initiated, this operation is brought to a conclusion.

To prevent the battery from being run down, a maximum number of 5 impulse memory recalls are allowed with the engine switched off, after this the recall requires continuous pressing. This number is reinitialized the moment the +VAN is interrupted or when the engine running information appears.

Memory recall sequence

The positioning of the seat is achieved through the following stages:

  • simultaneous sliding and raising adjustment,
  • then backrest adjustment.

The positioning of the rear view mirrors is managed by the NBC, the adjustment takes place in parallel at both rear view mirrors.

Acoustic warning device

An acoustic device is activated to improve the user's pereception when there is recourse to the memorizing functions. The acoustic signal used is the one for the NVO. The NAG makes an acoustic signal production request to the NBD via the connection at the VAN CAR 2 network.

The following cases are signalled:

  • recording of the memorizing of a position: 2 sounds are produced,
  • recording of the pressing of one of the memory recall controls: 1 sound is produced,
  • normal conclusion of a recall sequence for a position memorized: 1 sound is produced.

Standby and end of standby

Standby takes place when there is an interruption in the +VAN.

The NBC informs the NAG that there will be an interruption in the +VAN in the next 5 seconds. Having received this message, the NAG immediately stops any seat movement and memorizes the current position of the seat even if the user requests a manual control.

The NAB informs the NBC of the memorizing condition to either maintain the +VAN or not.

The end of standby takes place when the +VAN is present.

In standby, the NAG is not activated and cannot be activated by the NBC.

End of standby

The NAG exits the standy condition when the +VAN is present.

Operation in case of faults

If there is a problem, any memory recall by pressing briefly or for longer is inhibited.

If the +VAN is present, the seat can be operated directly using the manual controls. The NAG operates in local mode (predefined mode when the seat is fitted on the vehicle in the production plant).

If there is a problem, the memorizing cannot be carried out using the memorizing control panel or the remote control.

Safety

In memory recall situations, if the motors are not operated and the node does not identify any variation in the position for 2000ms ± 10ms for the rear view mirrors and 300ms ± 15ms or the seat, the operation of the motors is interrupted and the memory return continues for the other mechanisms as if the mechanism in question was in position.

In direct control situations, if the motors are operated and the node does not identify any variation in the position for 300ms ± 15ms for the seat motors, the node interrupts the operation of the motor. If pressed for more than 15 seconds ± 1 second, the node memorizes the fault. This action is stopped after the autodiagnosis and the elimination of the errors. If the fault disappears, the system becomes operational again.

If a memory recall button, except the memorizing button (M), is stuck in the button activated position, the control line is not available. Controls can be made using the other lines.

If an output is detected whilst a sensor does not identify any variation in position (and without a direct control or memory recall being requested), the system searches for the axis in question and activates the two outputs (this fault can occur, in particular, when a relay is stuck and the mechanism in question is in the end of travel position).

Seat motors

The maximum consumption for each motor below 13V, is between 20A at 23°C and 24A at -30°C

A thermal switch incorporated in the motor ensures that it does not remain in torque conditions for longer than 10 seconds.

Memorizing control

Memorizing is only possible if the +APC is present.

The memory recalls are recorded and remain valid as soon as the +VAN is detected.

The memorizing control panel switches are independent and operating a voltage levels. The current passing through the contacts is between 5 and 50mA (pull up resistance at electronic node).

Pressing either of button 1 or 2 is recorded and accepted even if the user has released button M.

Manual seat controls

The direct operation of the seat motors takes place via the contacts. The control takes place through voltage levels. The information is recorded and validated as soon as the +VAN is detected.

Seat sensors

The sensors used for identifying the positions are the impulse type, i.e. the identification of the position is relative.

The maximum consumption for each sensor is 15 mA. A current of between 2 and 5 mA circulates at the sensor output when it is low (node pull up resistance).

The power supply for the sensors is interrupted when the node is on standby (given that the mechanism is irreversible, there can be no movements if there is no power supply for the motors).

Rear view mirror sensors

The position sensors are the potentiometric type. There are two for each rear view mirror (one per axis).

The power supply for the sensors is interrupted when the node is in the standby position.

The variation in voltage supplied by the sensor is linear between each end of travel position.

The position sensor is a potentiometer of 3.7k%OHgr; ± 20% protected by a resistance of 1k%OHgr; ± 20%.

Diagnostics

The diagnostic function is designed to facilitate maintenance and indicate whether a component is defective: control switches, sensors, motors, relays and nodes.

The NAG carries out a fault diagnosis of the seat system and memorizes any faults.

The possible faults are:

  • when at least one of the motors should be activated (direct control or memory recall), the node detects no output activated,
  • a rear view mirror direct control switch is activated later in both directions and the node does not receive information concerning the movement of the sensor for one than one second in each direction when the corresponding output is activated (fault in the sensor or the rear view mirror motor),
  • a seat or column direct control switch is activated later in both directions and the node does not receive information concerning the movement of the sensor for one than 200ms in each direction when the corresponding output is activated (fault in the sensor or the seat or column motor),
  • the node receives information concerning the movement of a snesor without a direct control or memory recall having been made and without an output being activated (movement as a result of an electronic fault),
  • a memorizing request is not carried out correctly (memory fault).

Keeping a control panel button pressed for more than 180s ± 5s at the end of the memory recall procedure means that a message indicating that this button is stuck is recorded in the memory.

MANUAL CONTROLS

If a direct control switch is activated for more than 15 seconds and the node does not detect any movement of the sensor for the mechanism activated, the switch stuck fault messate is recorded in the non volatile memory (versions A, B or C: independent diagnostics).

LIST OF FAULTS

The possible faults are:

  • Electronic fault
  • Position measurement fault
  • Sliding sensor or motor fault
  • Backrest adjustment sensor or motor fault
  • Backrest height adjustment sensor or motor fault
  • Lifting adjustment sensor or motor fault
  • Seat adjustment sensor or motor fault
  • Relay no 1 fault (lifting)
  • Relay no 2 fault (joint lifting/backrest height)
  • Relay no 3 fault (backrest height)
  • Relay no 4 fault (sliding)
  • Relay no 5 fault (joing sliding/seat)
  • Relay no 6 fault (seat)
  • Relay no 8 fault (joint head restraint/backrest)
  • Relay no 9 fault (backrest)
  • Locking of a memorizing control panel switch
  • Locking of a seat direct control switch
  • Locking of a rear view mirror direct control switch
